item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"Both d1uc6a1 and d1o5dt2 are assigned to SCOPe family b.1.2.1, so the classification supports family-level homology; the fragment label on d1o5dt2 does not by itself create a separate family or imply greater evolutionary divergence. Align d1o5dt2 coverage-aware to the corresponding region of d1uc6a1, emphasizing the shared fibronectin type III core. Do not score absent fragment termini as insertions, deletions, or genuine sequence/structural variability, and beware that identity calculated only over a short overlap can be inflated. For a general family representative or a full-domain modeling template, prefer the more complete d1uc6a1 because it better represents domain length, topology, and boundary context. Retain d1o5dt2 when the sampled region or its particular biological context is specifically relevant, but do not use it alone as the canonical representative or as a template for unobserved portions. In diversity analyses, separate truncation and missing-coordinate effects from real variation, apply alignment-coverage thresholds, and avoid treating d1o5dt2's absent regions as evidence of unusual family architecture. Family membership supports homology, but neither the fragment annotation nor SCOPe classification alone justifies transferring an exact molecular function, binding specificity, or full-domain conformation; those claims require independent sequence, structural-coverage, and functional evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
